raw_case_text:
A 54-year-old Japanese man who had been diagnosed with RA for 8 years according to the 1987 American Rheumatism Association classification criteria for RA was admitted with polyarthritis. He complained of pain and swelling in the wrists, fingers, and knees and had difficulty walking without assistance. He claimed to have morning stiffness lasting about 3 hours. Past medical history included a left total knee arthroplasty complicated by a traumatic fracture of the left distal femur postoperatively and a cerebral infarction with residual right hemiparesis. His medication regimen included sulfasalazine (1000 mg/day), bucillamine (300 mg/day), mizoribine (150 mg/day), and prednisolone (10 mg/day). The Steinbrocker stage was IV and functional class was 4. He was unable to stand unassisted due to bilateral knee pain. Swelling and tenderness were present in the proximal interphalangeal and metacarpophalangeal joints of both hands and fingers, as well as in the wrists and knees. Right-sided muscle weakness was observed. Laboratory findings were as follows: white blood cell count 8800/mm3 (75.6% neutrophils, 19.5% lymphocytes, 2.9% monocytes, 0.3% eosinophils, 0.2% basophils), hemoglobin 10.7 mg/dL, platelets 48.7 x 104/muL, erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) 75 mm/h, C-reactive protein (CRP) 3.58 mg/dL, rheumatoid factor (RF) 219.6 IU/mL, and anticyclic citrullinated peptide antibody (ACPA) 189 IU/mL. Serum beta-D-glucan was negative. The purified protein derivative skin test for tuberculosis was negative. 
Treatment was initiated with subcutaneous injections of etanercept 25 mg twice a week. Blood samples were collected before the first dose (at baseline), 24 hours after the first injection (day 1), daily until day 8, and weekly thereafter. Specimens were centrifuged at 3000 rpm and the sera stored at -80 C until the assay was performed. TNF-alpha, TNFR-I and -II, IL-6, and IL-1 beta concentrations were measured using commercial ELISA kits.
After initiating etanercept, the patient's clinical condition improved markedly, with swelling and tenderness of the wrists and finger joints significantly better. He was able to stand with the aid of crutches despite residual hemiparesis. The duration of morning stiffness dropped to below 30 minutes. The 28-joint count Disease Activity Score (DAS28) dropped significantly within the first 4 weeks and continued to decrease (DAS28 = 8.09, 5.37, 4.73, and 4.60, at baseline, 4 weeks, 8 weeks, and 12 weeks, resp.), achieving the European League Against Rheumatism (EULAR) moderate response criteria. The CRP dropped to below 0.30 mg/mL within the first 2 weeks of therapy. Subsequently, the oral immunosuppressive regimen of sulfasalazine, bucillamine, and mizoribine was discontinued after initiation of treatment. Prednisolone was reduced to 5 mg/day.
After 12 weeks of treatment with etanercept, the patient developed a nonproductive cough along with a fever of 38 C. Serum beta-D-glucan was found to be positive, and sputum polymerase chain reaction (PCR) was positive for pneumocystis (Figure 1). Etanercept was discontinued, and an antifungal regimen initiated.
Preceding etanercept therapy, the serum IL-6 levels were found to be elevated, correlating with the high CRP value and high clinical disease activity. Conversely, the serum level of TNF-alpha was nondetectable (<0.2 pg/mL); the sTNFR-I, -II, and IL-1 beta values were not found to be significantly elevated (Figure 2). After initiation of etanercept, there was a rapid decline in the IL-6 and CRP levels, whereas the levels of TNF-alpha and sTNFR-II increased significantly within 24 hours after administration of the first dose to a plateau after 2 weeks (range: 100 pg/mL to 170 pg/mL) and 6-7 weeks (range: 300 ng/mL to 700 ng/mL), respectively. The sTNFR-I and IL-1-beta levels remained relatively unchanged (sTNFR-I levels at baseline, 3.56 ng/mL; 4 weeks, 3.36 ng/mL; 8 weeks, 2.93 ng/mL; 12 weeks, 3.58 ng/mL). At week 12, concurrent to the patient developing clinical symptoms of PCP, the levels of IL-6, CRP, and TNF-alpha showed an acute peak, which tapered downward over the following 3 weeks with the institution of an appropriate antifungal regimen (Figures 3 and 4).

subjective.chief_complaint: A 54-year-old Japanese man with an 8-year history of severe rheumatoid arthritis initially presented with disabling polyarthritis and 3-hour morning stiffness, and subsequently developed a nonproductive cough and fever (38 °C) after 12 weeks of etanercept therapy.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient was admitted with severe polyarthritis (Steinbrocker stage IV, functional class 4, baseline DAS28 8.09) involving the wrists, fingers, and knees, rendering him unable to stand unassisted. Subcutaneous etanercept (25 mg twice weekly) was initiated, resulting in rapid improvement in joint swelling/tenderness, reduction of morning stiffness to <30 minutes, and decline in DAS28 to 5.37 (week 4), 4.73 (week 8), and 4.60 (week 12), which allowed discontinuation of sulfasalazine, bucillamine, and mizoribine and reduction of prednisolone from 10 mg/day to 5 mg/day. At week 12 of etanercept therapy, he acutely developed a nonproductive cough and fever of 38 °C.
subjective.past_medical_history: Rheumatoid arthritis diagnosed 8 years prior (Steinbrocker stage IV, class 4); left total knee arthroplasty complicated by postoperative traumatic fracture of the left distal femur; cerebral infarction with residual right hemiparesis.
subjective.review_of_systems: Baseline positive for polyarthralgia, joint swelling, and 3-hour morning stiffness; week 12 positive for nonproductive cough and fever (38 °C). Baseline medications included sulfasalazine (1,000 mg/day), bucillamine (300 mg/day), mizoribine (150 mg/day), and prednisolone (10 mg/day, tapered to 5 mg/day after starting etanercept).

objective.physical_examination: Baseline examination: Swelling and tenderness of bilateral PIP, MCP, wrist, and knee joints; inability to stand unassisted; residual right-sided hemiparesis. At week 12 of etanercept therapy: Febrile at 38.0 °C with nonproductive cough.
objective.routine_investigations: Baseline pre-etanercept laboratory tests: WBC 8,800/mm3 (75.6% neutrophils, 19.5% lymphocytes, 2.9% monocytes, 0.3% eosinophils, 0.2% basophils), hemoglobin 10.7 g/dL, platelets 48.7 x 10^4/μL, ESR 75 mm/h, C-reactive protein (CRP) 3.58 mg/dL (dropping to <0.30 mg/dL by week 2 before spiking at week 12), rheumatoid factor (RF) 219.6 IU/mL, anti-CCP antibody (ACPA) 189 IU/mL, and negative tuberculin PPD skin test.
objective.advanced_workup: Serial cytokine profiling (ELISA): Baseline elevated serum IL-6 with undetectable TNF-alpha (<0.2 pg/mL) and unremarkable sTNFR-I (3.56 ng/mL), sTNFR-II, and IL-1beta; following etanercept initiation, IL-6 and CRP fell rapidly while circulating TNF-alpha (100–170 pg/mL) and sTNFR-II (300–700 ng/mL) rose to a plateau, followed at week 12 (coinciding with PCP onset) by an acute surge in serum IL-6, CRP, and TNF-alpha. Fungal biomarker and molecular microbiology at week 12: Serum beta-D-glucan converted from negative at baseline to positive, and sputum polymerase chain reaction (PCR) tested positive for Pneumocystis jirovecii.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PCP) developing 12 weeks after initiating etanercept therapy for rheumatoid arthritis, confirmed by positive sputum Pneumocystis PCR and seroconversion of serum beta-D-glucan, accompanied by a simultaneous acute spike in serum IL-6, CRP, and TNF-alpha. Plan and clinical course: Etanercept was immediately discontinued and targeted anti-Pneumocystis therapy was instituted, leading to clinical recovery and downward tapering of IL-6, CRP, and TNF-alpha levels over the subsequent 3 weeks.
